chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from al-Abbas ibn Amir, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
He (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not take possession of what you specify.' He means: Do not specify it and then take possession of what is due to you from it.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report is to be understood as referring to a type of dislike (karahah), because we have clarified that it is permissible for a person to take from what he has specified, and there is no contradiction between the reports.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to specify and then take possession of an item in a sale according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) advises against the practice of specifying a debt item and then immediately taking possession of it, a nuance that commentator Muhammad ibn al-Hasan interprets as *karahah* (dislike) rather than absolute prohibition (*haram*). This scholarly resolution harmonizes the text with other hadiths permitting such sales, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of avoiding contradiction between narrations while preserving the preferred etiquette of transactional clarity.
